title: Study Smarter With The Pomodoro Method
description: A simple focus method to help you study without burning out.

scenes.text: Struggling to focus while studying? Try this simple method used by millions of students.
It's called the Pomodoro technique. Set a timer for twenty five minutes and work on just one task.
No phone, no extra tabs, no distractions. Just you and the task until the timer rings.
Then take a five minute break. Stretch, drink some water, and look away from the screen.
After four rounds, take a longer break of fifteen to thirty minutes.
Short bursts of focus beat long, tired hours. Try one round today and follow for more study tips.

title: Stop Re-Reading Your Notes! Do This Instead
description: Active recall is one of the most effective ways to study.

scenes.text: Re-reading your notes feels productive, but it's one of the weakest ways to study.
A better way is active recall. Close the book and try to write down everything you remember.
Struggling to remember is the point. That effort is what makes memories stronger.
Check your notes, fix the gaps, and then test yourself again.
Flashcards and practice questions are easy ways to do this every day.
Test yourself more and re-read less. Try it for your next exam, and follow for more tips.

title: Why You Forget Everything After Cramming
description: Spaced repetition helps you remember what you study for longer.

scenes.text: Why do we forget what we study so fast? Because we cram everything into one night.
Spaced repetition fixes this. Review the same topic after one day, then three days, then a week.
Each review tells your brain that this information matters, so it stays longer.
Apps like Anki can schedule reviews for you, or you can simply use a calendar.
Ten minutes of review spread across the week beats three hours of cramming.
Plan your reviews today and thank yourself later. Follow for more study tips.

title: The Feynman Trick To Know If You Really Understand
description: Explain it simply to find out what you really know.

scenes.text: Here's a trick to find out if you really understand something.
Pick a topic and explain it in simple words, as if you were teaching a ten year old.
Where you get stuck or use big confusing words, that's where you don't understand it yet.
Go back to your notes, learn that part, and explain it again, simpler this time.
If you can explain it simply, you truly know it.
Try this with your hardest topic today, and follow for more.

title: Why All Nighters Before Exams Backfire
description: Sleep is part of studying. Here's why.

scenes.text: Pulling an all nighter before an exam? That may hurt you more than it helps.
Sleep is when your brain sorts and stores what you learned during the day.
Without enough sleep, it's harder to focus, remember things, and stay calm.
Keep a steady sleep schedule, and stay away from screens for the last hour before bed.
Finish studying earlier and sleep well. Your exam brain will thank you.
Good sleep is a study tip too. Follow for more.

title: Your Phone Is Killing Your Focus
description: A simple rule to stop phone distractions while studying.

scenes.text: Your phone is the biggest enemy of your focus.
Even a buzz on the table can pull your attention away from your work.
Put your phone in another room while you study, or at least turn on do not disturb.
Use it as a reward after your study block instead of a constant interruption.
You'll finish faster and feel less tired.
Try one phone free hour today, and follow for more study tips.

title: Plan Tomorrow Tonight For An Easier Morning
description: A two minute habit that makes your day easier.

scenes.text: Want an easier morning? Plan your day the night before.
Write down the top three tasks you must finish tomorrow.
When you wake up, you won't waste time deciding what to do.
Keep your bag, notes, and water bottle ready so you can start right away.
Starting is the hardest part, and a plan makes it simple.
Take two minutes tonight to plan tomorrow. Follow for more.

title: Eat The Frog: Beat Procrastination
description: Do the hardest task first and everything else gets easier.

scenes.text: Do you keep putting off your hardest task? Here's a simple rule.
Do the hardest or most important task first, when your energy is highest.
People call it eating the frog. Once it's done, everything else feels easier.
Don't check messages or social media before you begin.
Even thirty focused minutes on the hard task is a big win.
So, what's your frog for today? Follow for more productivity tips.

title: Stuck While Studying? Do This For 5 Minutes
description: A short walk can help you reset your focus.

scenes.text: Feeling stuck while studying? Don't just stare at the page.
Stand up and take a short walk for five minutes.
Moving your body and getting fresh air can help you reset and think more clearly.
Leave your phone behind so your mind can really rest.
Then come back and start again with a clear head.
A short break can save you hours. Follow for more.

title: Don't Study On An Empty Stomach
description: Simple food and water habits for better focus.

scenes.text: Your brain needs fuel, so don't study on an empty stomach.
Drink water regularly, because being dehydrated can make it harder to concentrate.
Keep simple snacks like fruit or nuts near your desk instead of chips.
Eat regular meals so your energy stays steady through the day.
Small habits like these make long study sessions easier.
Drink a glass of water right now, and follow for more.
Think you're good at multitasking? Your brain says otherwise.
Switching between tasks makes you slower and more likely to make mistakes.
Pick one task, close everything else, and work on it until it's done.
Keep a notebook nearby to jot down random thoughts, then get back to your task.
One task at a time feels slower, but it finishes faster.
Try single tasking for one session today. Follow for more.

title: The 2 Minute Rule To Start Studying

scenes.text: Can't get yourself to start studying? Use the two minute rule.
Tell yourself you'll study for just two minutes, nothing more.
Open your book, read one page, or solve one question.
Starting is the hardest part. Once you begin, it's easier to keep going.
And if you stop after two minutes, you still did more than nothing.
Start your two minutes now, and follow for more study tips.
